He must keep the solemnity of tabernacles, so as to hasten from the tabernacle to the courts of God, and from the courts to the house, and from the house to the temple.
50_marg3648: Jerusalem, that is, the Church, is not in low places, but set on a mountain, so that it can be seen from every side. So whoever wishes to adore the Lord, let him go up to the mountains. But whoever is of the families of the land, that is, weighed down by some business of earthly life, and therefore cannot adore God on the mountains, his land is not watered by the rains of heaven.
50_marg3649: The Jews hope that all these things will come in the flesh, promising themselves circumcision and marriages in the empire of a thousand years, lest the curse which the law pronounces on the barren should be fulfilled in them.
50_marg3650: As long as anyone remains an Egyptian or a heathen he cannot raise his step to the heights, and therefore lacks God’s rain; and this will be the greatest sin for the Egyptian and the Assyrian, the Chaldean, the Syrian, the Moabite and the other nations, if they will not go out of their lands, so as to cease to be men and, made Israelites in whom there is no guile, go up to Jerusalem, that through the tabernacles they may come to the eternal house.

50_marg3651: In that day that which is upon the bridle of the horse, and so on. According to the letter: in the time of the everlasting solemnity and of the kingdom of Jerusalem, all being at peace, there will be no need of cavalry, but all the adornment and beauty of the trappings is to be given to the worship of God; and as many flock together from every side to the sacrifices, the caldrons will be constantly in the service of the sacrifices, as the phials are wont to shine constantly before the altar; nor will any caldron be dedicated to another use.
50_marg3652: When the caldrons have been turned into phials, then those who are left of all the nations will boil the flesh of the victims, so as not to eat raw flesh, but that all the moisture may be cooked out; nor will there be need of a merchant to carry wares from place to place.
50_marg3653: By the horses the madness of lust is understood; by the bridles, the word of God, made of the gold of wisdom and the silver of eloquence. By this bridle the lustful man is held back so as not to fall headlong, but, going on a straight road, to offer the Lord a soft back to sit on, and to be consecrated, ready, to his worship. And the caldrons in which the flesh of the sacrifices was boiled are turned into phials, because those who understood in a fleshly way, turned from the sacrifices of the law to spiritual understanding, become lamps burning and shining in the house of God.
50_marg3654: When the minds of believers have been turned into spiritual phials to receive the various spices of the virtues, then those who offer God the sacrifice of praise will cook it with the fire of the Holy Spirit; nor will there be a merchant in the house of prayer, for the Lord cast out of his Church those who bought and sold, and so on.
